summary: Tenant-induced pipeline IO spill causing autoscaler latency and p99 throughput degradation in reserved pool
description: Issue summary: Multiple LexiHealth tenants on reserved capacity experienced sudden p99 throughput regressions and elevated tail latency beginning 2026-03-10 14:12 UTC. Symptoms include stalled batch queues, autoscaler taking 30-90s to react, and error bursts of 502/504 on long streaming requests. Impact: LexiHealth reported degraded user-facing response times for inference flows tied to clinical note summarization, causing timeouts and retries in their app. Timeline: 14:12 UTC spike in IO wait and NVMe device queue depth observed; autoscaler attempted scale-up but new allocations delayed due to slot fragmentation; 14:27 UTC temporary mitigation applied (tenant soft-rate-limit). Hypothesis: A noisy tenant generated high small-request fanout (many short streams) that induced storage-io pressure on the node local NVMe, which cascaded into serving runtime stalls and autoscaler misjudging available capacity leading to delayed allocations and p99 throughput loss. Next steps: continue root-cause data collection (iostat, container-level io stats), validate autoscaler sampling windows, and evaluate a short-term tenant-level soft cap plus scheduler affinity tweak.
impact: Customer production traffic experiencing p99 latency increases from ~1.1s to ~7-12s on long-context streaming endpoints and increased 5xx rate (~4% of requests). Business impact: customer-facing app timeouts and retries affecting clinical workflows for a subset of users.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Route sustained small (<=128 token) streaming requests from many concurrent clients (1000+ short streams) to a single reserved pool with mixed tenant placement.
2) Observe NVMe device queue depth and host-level i/o util increase in affected nodes.
3) Watch batcher queues grow and p99 token latency climb; autoscaler logs show scale decision but allocation delayed due to fragmented GPU slot availability.
4) Reproduce with isolated synthetic load in staging by replaying LexiHealth request trace (attached).
investigation_notes: Checked node metrics: affected hosts show NVMe write queue saturated and high iowait correlated with request spikes.
Correlation found between many short streaming sessions from a single tenant and NVMe random I/O spike (small writes for logging/checkpointing in sidecars).
Autoscaler sampling window (30s) + allocation TPS limits caused scale decisions to be queued; combined with GPU slot fragmentation, allocations were delayed 30-90s.
No kernel panic or driver OOM; memory usage normal. Evidence of a background sidecar on tenant containers performing frequent small fsyncs during request processing.
Heatmap from 2026-03-10 14:00-14:30 UTC attached in Confluence (see link).
comments: Ava Chen (Support) 2026-03-10: Customer reported p99 jump at 14:15 UTC. Escalating to SRE and Dedicated infra on-call.
Diego Martinez (SRE) 2026-03-10: Observed NVMe queue spike on nodes hosting LexiHealth shards. Kicking off node-level io captures and sampling container io stats.
Maya Patel (Infra Eng) 2026-03-11: Identified a LexiHealth sidecar that writes frequent small checkpoints. Requesting customer to temporarily disable sidecar while we test scheduler affinity change.
LexiHealth-SRE (customer) 2026-03-11: Can disable sidecar for a 30-min window at 15:00 UTC. Asking for recommended mitigation until permanent fix.
Diego Martinez (SRE) 2026-03-11: Applied temporary tenant soft-rate-limit (50% of baseline) and bumped reserved pool by +1 GPU as short-term mitigation. Monitoring.
Ava Chen (Support) 2026-03-13: Customer confirmed reduced 5xx and p99 latency returned closer to baseline after mitigation. Planning follow-up for permanent remediation.
resolution: Mitigation applied: (1) Tenant soft-rate-limit deployed for LexiHealth at 2026-03-11 15:02 UTC, (2) temporary +1 GPU reservation added to affected pool, (3) customer disabled sidecar during mitigation window. Result: p99 latency reduced from ~10s to ~1.4s and 5xx dropped below 0.5%. Permanent fix path: implement scheduler placement preference to avoid collocating high-small-io tenants, add per-tenant burst IO throttling at node-local level, and adjust autoscaler to consider IO wait metrics when deciding scaling. Owner: Diego Martinez. Follow-up task INT-468042 created for infra changes.
